c.tagline: Germany's harbor city of red brick, canals, and Reeperbahn nights.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; hail one at ranks, on the street, or via the Free Now app. A ride across the centre runs roughly 10-15 EUR.

emergency.note: 112 reaches ambulance and fire across the EU; 110 is the direct police line. Both are free from any phone.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: St. Pauli/Reeperbahn nightlife — watch for scams, pickpockets and aggressive touts

hood_desc: Hamburg's walkable core around the Rathaus, Jungfernstieg and the Binnenalster lake, blending the historic Altstadt with the shopping and business streets of Neustadt; best for first-timers who want everything within reach.

The city's raucous nightlife district built around the Reeperbahn, Europe's longest strip of bars, clubs and live-music venues, plus the Sunday fish market; suits travelers who want to go out late and stay in the thick of it.
A trendy, left-leaning quarter of street art, indie boutiques, cafes and buzzing bars just north of Altona; a former counterculture stronghold that draws a younger, alternative crowd.
Hamburg's sleek modern waterfront district on former docklands beside the Speicherstadt warehouses, anchored by the Elbphilharmonie concert hall, with design hotels, promenades and quiet river views.
A formerly independent town turned laid-back local district west of the centre, full of shops, restaurants, the Altona fish market and Elbe-side parks; a relaxed base for seeing everyday Hamburg.
lodging: Hotel Domicil Hamburg by Golden Tulip

water.note: Tap water is safe and of high quality.

transit.hours: U-Bahn and S-Bahn run roughly 4:30am-1am on weekdays and all night on Friday and Saturday nights; night buses cover the gaps midweek.
transit.pay: There are no tap-in gates: buy tickets in the hvv app or from station machines (cards accepted) and have them ready before boarding. A Hamburg AB single costs about 4.10 EUR (~US$4.50) and a day ticket about 8.20 EUR; one ticket covers U-Bahn, S-Bahn, buses and the public harbour ferries. App tickets usually get a ~7% discount, and the Deutschland-Ticket (63 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.

transit.m: S-Bahn S1 to Jungfernstieg city centre (30 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% for good service is customary. Tell the server the total you want to pay as you hand over the money.
